title: The one-element case of lifting a Popescu resolution.
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring, $A$ a finitely presented $R$-algebra, $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra, $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra map and $q$ a prime of $\Lambda$. Resolution and strict standardness mean [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution] and [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]. For a list $\pi$ indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}(r)$, require all elements to map into $q$, multiplication by $\pi_i$ and $\pi_i^2$ to have equal kernels on $R$ and $\Lambda$ modulo preceding eighth powers, and all images in $A$ to be strictly standard. The final quotient map commutes with $\alpha$ and its prime pulls back to $q$. For $r=1$, assertion $P(1)$ of [def-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-induction] holds.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F8, proof

proof.text: (Singular ideals map into singular ideals under base change; written out for the verification Stacks leaves implicit in the case $r=1$.) Let $R\to A$ be a ring map, $R\to R'$ a ring map and $A'=A\otimes_RR'$. Then the image of $H_{A/R}$ in $A'$ lies in $H_{A'/R'}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. Indeed let $g\in A$ with $A_g$ smooth over $R$. Then $R'\to A_g\otimes_RR'$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](1). Since $A\to A_g$ is a localization at $\{g^n\}$, the map $A'\to A'\otimes_AA_g$ is the localization of $A'$ at the powers of $g\otimes1$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], and $A'\otimes_AA_g=(R'\otimes_RA)\otimes_AA_g\cong R'\otimes_RA_g$ as $R'$-algebras (associativity of the tensor product). Hence $A'_{g\otimes1}$ is smooth over $R'$, i.e. $g\otimes1$ lies in the set $G'$ of [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] for $R'\to A'$. So the image of the ideal generated by $G$ lies in the ideal generated by $G'$, and if $h\in H_{A/R}=\sqrt{(G)}$, say $h^n\in(G)$, then $(h\otimes1)^n\in(G')$, so $h\otimes1\in\sqrt{(G')}=H_{A'/R'}$. We use it with $R'=R/\pi^8R$, $A'=A/\pi^8A$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change]: the image of $H_{A/R}\Lambda$ in $\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ lies in $H_{\bar A/\bar R}\cdot\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ (both maps to $\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ are compatible), hence the image of $\mathfrak h_A$ lies in $\mathfrak h_{\bar A}$ (images of radical elements are radical over the image).

proof.text: (Case $r=1$: lifting the resolution.) Write $\pi=\pi_1$, $\bar R=R/\pi^8R$, $\bar A=A/\pi^8A$, $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$, $\bar{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q/\pi^8\Lambda$. By hypothesis there is a resolution $\bar A\to\bar C\to\bar\Lambda$ of $\bar R\to\bar A\to\bar\Lambda\supset\bar{\mathfrak q}$: $\bar C$ is of finite presentation over $\bar R$ and $\mathfrak h_{\bar A}\subset\mathfrak h_{\bar C}\not\subset\bar{\mathfrak q}$. Hypothesis (1) for $i=1$ (the ideal $(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_0^8)$ is $0$) says $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$ and $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)$; hypothesis (2) for $i=1$ says $\pi$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$; $R$ is Noetherian and $A$ of finite presentation. So [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-desingularize-lifting-apply] (Stacks 07F0) applies to $A\to\Lambda$ and the factorization $\bar A\to\bar C\to\bar\Lambda$ and gives a factorization $A\to B\to\Lambda$ with $B$ of finite presentation over $R$, $R_\pi\to B_\pi$ smooth, and $H_{\bar C/\bar R}\bar\Lambda\subset(\mathfrak h_B+\pi^8\Lambda)/\pi^8\Lambda$, where $\mathfrak h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}\Lambda}$. We show in steps 3-4 that $A\to B\to\Lambda$ is a resolution of $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$.

proof.text: ($\pi\in\mathfrak h_B$, hence $\pi^8\Lambda\subset\mathfrak h_B$.) Let $g$ be the image of $\pi$ in $B$. The map $R\to R$ is smooth (polynomial ring in $0$ variables [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth]), so $R\to R_\pi$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization]; $B_\pi=B\otimes_RR_\pi$ is the localization $B_g$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], and $R_\pi\to B_g$ is smooth by step 2, so the composite $R\to R_\pi\to B_g$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](2). Hence $g\in H_{B/R}$ by [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], so the image of $\pi$ in $\Lambda$ lies in $H_{B/R}\Lambda\subset\mathfrak h_B$, and $\pi^8\Lambda\subset\mathfrak h_B$. Consequently $(\mathfrak h_B+\pi^8\Lambda)/\pi^8\Lambda=\mathfrak h_B/\pi^8\Lambda$, a radical ideal of $\bar\Lambda$ (its preimage $\mathfrak h_B$ is radical), and step 2 gives $H_{\bar C/\bar R}\bar\Lambda\subset\mathfrak h_B/\pi^8\Lambda$, hence $\mathfrak h_{\bar C}=\sqrt{H_{\bar C/\bar R}\bar\Lambda}\subset\mathfrak h_B/\pi^8\Lambda$: every $\lambda\in\Lambda$ whose class lies in $\mathfrak h_{\bar C}$ lies in $\mathfrak h_B$.
